en: to possess both; to have both

examples.ko: 그 선수는 실력과 인성을 겸비해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That player has both skill and character, so he is very popular.

examples.ko: 지혜와 용기를 겸비한 사람이 리더가 돼야 해요.
examples.en: A person with both wisdom and courage should become the leader.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 디자인과 기능을 겸비한 제품을 만들어요.
examples.en: This company makes products that combine design and function.

examples.ko: 외모와 실력을 모두 겸비하기는 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It is not easy to have both looks and talent.
She has both talent and virtue, so she is respected.

examples.ko: 이 카페는 맛과 분위기를 모두 겸비했어요.
examples.en: This cafe has both good taste and a good atmosphere.

explain: 보통 'A와 B를 겸비하다'처럼 좋은 점 두 가지 이상을 함께 가졌을 때 칭찬하는 말이에요. 나쁜 점에는 쓰지 않고, '갖추다'보다 글이나 격식 있는 말투에서 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is usually used as 'A와 B를 겸비하다' to praise someone or something for having two or more good qualities together. It is not used for bad qualities, and it sounds more formal or written than '갖추다'.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 함께 이 책을 공저했어요.
examples.en: The two of them co-authored this book.
I decided to co-write a travel essay book with a friend.
I take the class with a textbook the professors co-authored.
Several writers co-wrote it, so the voices are varied.

examples.ko: 선배와 논문을 공저하면 많이 배울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you co-author a paper with a senior, you can learn a lot.
Someday I'd like to co-write a cookbook with my family.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '같이 썼어요'라고 하고, '공저하다'는 책이나 논문을 소개할 때 써요. 책이나 논문 같은 글을 대상으로 하는 격식 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: In daily talk people say '같이 썼어요', while '공저하다' is used when introducing books or papers. It is a formal word used for written works such as books and papers.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 한국어 구사력이 아주 뛰어나요.
examples.en: That singer's command of Korean is outstanding.

examples.ko: 외국어 구사력을 키우려면 말을 많이 해 봐야 해요.
examples.en: To build your skill in using a foreign language, you have to speak a lot.
They also evaluate your English ability in the interview.

examples.ko: 말하기 구사력은 연습한 만큼 꼭 늘어요.
examples.en: Your speaking skill definitely grows as much as you practice.

examples.ko: 영어 구사력에 자신이 생겨서 발표를 신청했어요.
examples.en: I gained confidence in my English, so I signed up to give a presentation.
For an international student's Korean, it is surprisingly natural.

explain: 주로 '영어 구사력', '한국어 구사력'처럼 언어를 실제로 쓰는 능력에 써요. 단어를 아는 것보다 상황에 맞게 말하고 쓰는 힘을 가리켜요. '실력'보다 말과 표현에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It is mainly used for the ability to actually use a language, as in '영어 구사력' or '한국어 구사력'. It points to using words well in context rather than just knowing them. Compared with '실력', the focus is on speech and expression.

examples.en: My friend speaks Korean naturally.
The player used a variety of techniques.

examples.ko: 외국어를 잘 구사하려면 매일 말해 봐야 해요.
examples.en: To use a foreign language well, you have to speak it every day.

examples.ko: 그 작가는 아름다운 표현을 구사하는 것으로 유명해요.
examples.en: That writer is famous for using beautiful expressions.

examples.ko: 세 나라 말을 구사할 수 있는 직원을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: We're looking for an employee who can speak three languages.

examples.ko: 감독은 새로운 작전을 구사해서 경기를 이겼어요.
examples.en: The coach used a new strategy and won the game.

explain: 언어, 기술, 전술, 표현을 능숙하게 쓸 때 써요. 단순히 '쓰다'보다 솜씨가 좋다는 칭찬 느낌이 있어요. '한국어를 구사하다'는 말하는 실력이 좋다는 뜻으로 많이 들려요.
explain_en: Use it when someone handles a language, skill, tactic, or expression with ease. Compared with plain 쓰다, it carries a hint of praise for skill. '한국어를 구사하다' is a common way to say someone speaks Korean well.

examples.en: My father worked diligently all his life.
A diligent person earns trust anywhere.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 근면해서 지각을 한 번도 안 했어요.
examples.en: That friend is diligent and has never once been late.

examples.ko: 근면하다고 해서 꼭 성공하는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being diligent doesn't necessarily mean you will succeed.

examples.ko: 신입 사원이 근면하고 성실해서 칭찬을 많이 받아요.
examples.en: The new employee is diligent and sincere, so he gets a lot of praise.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 근면하셨기 때문에 가난을 이겨 낼 수 있었어요.
examples.en: Grandfather was able to overcome poverty because he was diligent.

explain: '부지런하다'가 일상에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이고, '근면하다'는 글이나 칭찬하는 말에 더 어울려요. '근면 성실'처럼 '성실'과 같이 쓰는 일이 많고, 반대말은 '게으르다'예요.
explain_en: '부지런하다' is the more casual everyday word, while '근면하다' suits writing and words of praise. It is often paired with '성실' as in '근면 성실', and its opposite is '게으르다' (lazy).

examples.en: He has a gift for writing, so his blog is popular.

examples.ko: 저는 글재주가 없어서 편지 쓰기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: I have no writing talent, so writing letters is hard for me.

examples.ko: 글재주만 믿고 연습을 안 하면 실력이 늘지 않아요.
examples.en: If you rely only on your talent and don't practice, you won't improve.
My younger sibling has had an exceptional way with words since childhood.

examples.ko: 글재주는 타고나기도 하지만 많이 써 보면 늘어요.
examples.en: Writing talent can be innate, but it grows if you write a lot.

examples.ko: 언니의 글재주 덕분에 공모전에서 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my sister's writing talent, we won a prize at the contest.

explain: 보통 '글재주가 있다/없다'로 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '글솜씨'도 많이 쓰는데, '글재주'는 타고난 재능이라는 느낌이 더 있어요.
explain_en: It is usually said as '글재주가 있다/없다' (have/lack writing talent). '글솜씨' is a similar word that is also common, but '글재주' sounds a bit more like an innate gift.

en: to take over; to snag (a position)

examples.ko: 그는 입사 3년 만에 팀장 자리를 꿰찼어요.
examples.en: He snagged the team leader position after only three years at the company.
A rookie has taken a starting spot, and it's the talk of the town.
It's amazing that the youngest landed the lead role.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 우리 동네 맛집 1위를 꿰차고 있어요.
examples.en: That shop holds the number one spot among restaurants in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 좋은 자리를 꿰차려고 다들 경쟁하고 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone is competing to grab a good position.

examples.ko: 어느새 사장 자리를 꿰찬 사람이 누구예요?
examples.en: Who is the person who has taken the president's seat before anyone noticed?

explain: '차지하다'와 비슷하지만 좋은 자리나 역할을 능력이나 수완으로 자기 것으로 만들었다는 느낌이 강해요. 주로 '자리를 꿰차다', '주전을 꿰차다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '차지하다' but suggests someone won a good position or role through skill or maneuvering. It usually appears as '자리를 꿰차다' or '주전을 꿰차다'.

en: to be diligent; to be industrious

examples.en: My grandmother moves around busily from early morning.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 정말 바지런해서 일을 금방 끝내요.
examples.en: That friend is really diligent and finishes work quickly.

examples.ko: 바지런한 이웃 덕분에 골목이 늘 깨끗해요.
examples.en: Thanks to a diligent neighbor, the alley is always clean.

examples.ko: 동생은 바지런해서 쉬는 날에도 가만히 있지 않아요.
examples.en: My sibling is so industrious that he never sits still even on days off.
If you work diligently, the day goes by quickly.
My mother is industrious, so she even tends the garden herself.

explain: '부지런하다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 일을 미루지 않고 몸을 잘 움직이는 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요. 반대말은 '게으르다'예요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '부지런하다'. You use it to praise someone who doesn't put work off and keeps active. The opposite is '게으르다'.

en: to be selected; to be chosen

examples.en: That rookie actor was picked for the lead role.

examples.ko: 제 친구가 이번에 대표팀 선수로 발탁됐대요.
examples.en: I heard my friend was selected for the national team this time.

examples.ko: 새 팀장으로 발탁된 분이 인사하러 왔어요.
examples.en: The person chosen as the new team leader came to say hello.

examples.ko: 사장님의 눈에 띄어서 중요한 일에 발탁될 수 있었어요.
examples.en: I caught the boss's eye and was able to be chosen for an important task.

examples.ko: 길에서 발탁돼서 모델이 된 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people were scouted on the street and became models.
After being picked, I practiced even harder.

explain: '발탁되다'는 여러 사람 중에서 능력을 인정받아 뽑혀 중요한 자리에 오르는 거예요. 단순히 뽑히는 '선택되다'보다 기회를 얻는 느낌이 강해요. 능동형 '발탁하다'는 뽑는 사람이 주어예요.
explain_en: 발탁되다 means being chosen from many people because your ability is recognized and getting an important role. It feels like getting an opportunity more than the plain 선택되다. The active form 발탁하다 has the person doing the choosing as its subject.

dis.h: picked from many for a key role

p.n: 발탁되다 stresses being singled out above others; 선발되다 stresses passing a selection process.

examples.en: I set down a step stool to reach the high shelf.

examples.ko: 현관 앞 발판에 신발의 흙을 털었어요.
examples.en: I shook the dirt off my shoes on the mat at the front door.
This footboard is slippery, so it is dangerous.

examples.ko: 버스에 오를 때 발판이 높아서 조심했어요.
examples.en: The step was high when I boarded the bus, so I was careful.

examples.ko: 그는 이번 성공을 발판 삼아 더 크게 도전했어요.
examples.en: He took on a bigger challenge using this success as a stepping stone.
I put my foot on the bicycle pedal.

explain: 발이 닿는 판이라는 뜻에서 계단, 받침, 문 앞 매트까지 넓게 써요. 비유로는 '발판이 되다', '발판으로 삼다'처럼 다음 단계로 가는 기반이라는 뜻이 있어요.

phrases.example: 이번 경험을 발판으로 삼아 더 높은 목표에 도전할래요.
phrases.en: to use as a stepping stone
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 발판이 아니라 다음 성공을 위한 바탕으로 쓴다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not mean a real platform but using something as a base for the next success.

explain_en: The word covers anything your foot rests on, from a step or footrest to a doormat. Figuratively, '발판이 되다' and '발판으로 삼다' mean a base for reaching the next stage.

en: to be displayed; to be exhibited

examples.en: My usual ability showed well on the exam.
His leadership came through in the crisis.
Children's creativity comes out when they feel free.
I was nervous, so my strength didn't come out.

examples.ko: 이 약의 효과는 한 시간 뒤에 발휘될 거예요.
examples.en: This medicine's effect will kick in after an hour.

examples.ko: 응원을 받으니까 실력이 더 발휘되는 것 같아요.
examples.en: With people cheering, it feels like my skills come out better.

explain: 능력이 밖으로 나타날 때 써요. 사람이 일부러 보여 주면 '발휘하다', 저절로 드러나면 '발휘되다'를 써요. '실력', '힘', '효과'처럼 능력을 주어로 하는 문장이 많아요.
explain_en: It describes an ability coming out. When a person deliberately shows it, use 발휘하다, and when it simply shows up, 발휘되다. Subjects are usually abilities, such as 실력, 힘, or 효과.

examples.en: I am studying ecology at university.

examples.ko: 생태학 수업 시간에 숲을 직접 관찰했어요.
examples.en: In ecology class, we observed a forest firsthand.

examples.ko: 동생은 생태학을 전공해서 연구소에서 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling majors in ecology and wants to work at a research institute.

examples.ko: 생태학 교수님이 강에 사는 물고기를 조사하러 가셨어요.
examples.en: The ecology professor went to survey the fish living in the river.

examples.ko: 이 책은 생태학에 관심이 있는 사람들에게 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This book is popular with people interested in ecology.
Ecologists analyzed why the number of migratory birds has dropped.

explain: '생태계'와 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. '생태학'은 학문 이름이고, '생태계'는 자연 속 생물들의 관계 그 자체를 말해요. '생태 공원', '생태 관광'처럼 '생태'만 앞에 붙여서도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It helps to learn it together with '생태계' (ecosystem): '생태학' is the name of the academic field, while '생태계' refers to the web of living things in nature itself. '생태' alone is also often attached in front, as in '생태 공원' or '생태 관광'.

en: to be selected; to be picked

examples.en: I was selected as a representative player.

examples.ko: 열 명 중에서 두 명이 선발되었어요.
examples.en: Two out of ten were selected.
The selected students will meet next week.

examples.ko: 시험을 잘 보면 선발될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you do well on the test, you can be selected.
They give a prize to the people who are selected.
I failed the test and was not selected.

explain: '뽑히다'는 일상에서 쓰는 말이고, '선발되다'는 대회·장학금·팀처럼 공식적인 선택에 써요. 뽑는 쪽은 '선발하다'예요. 일자리를 얻는 일은 '채용되다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '뽑히다' is everyday, while '선발되다' is for official selection such as competitions, scholarships, and teams. The choosing side uses '선발하다'. For getting a job, '채용되다' is more natural.

dis.h: picked via exam or competition; team, staff

p.n: 선정되다 only says chosen after review; 선발되다 implies competition or testing.

examples.en: He carried out his role just as well as anyone could.

examples.ko: 중고차인데 새 차처럼 손색없이 잘 달려요.
examples.en: It's a used car, but it runs as well as a new one.

examples.ko: 아이들이 어른 못지않게 손색없이 공연을 마쳤어요.
examples.en: The children finished the performance just as well as adults.
This space has been decorated so well that it could easily pass as a café.
Everything has been prepared so well that I have no worries.

examples.ko: 한복이 모델과 비교해도 손색없이 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: The hanbok looks just as good as it would on a model.

explain: '손색없이 해내다', '손색없이 꾸미다'처럼 동작이나 결과가 기준에 뒤지지 않을 때 써요. 형용사 '손색없다'를 부사로 바꾼 말이에요. 말할 때보다 칭찬하는 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used with actions or results that don't fall short of a standard, such as '손색없이 해내다' or '손색없이 꾸미다'. It is the adverb form of the adjective '손색없다'. You'll see it more in praising writing and news than in casual speech.

en: to complete (a course or training program); to graduate from a program

examples.en: I completed the Korean course.
I finish the training program this month.

examples.ko: 과정을 수료하면 증명서를 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you complete the program, you can get a certificate.
The students who completed the course took photos.

examples.ko: 석사 과정을 수료하고 논문을 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: I finished the master's coursework and am writing my thesis.

examples.ko: 열 번 이상 결석하면 수료할 수 없어요.
examples.en: If you miss ten or more classes, you cannot complete it.

explain: 수료는 정해진 과정을 끝까지 마쳤다는 표현이고, 졸업은 학교의 전체 과정을 마치고 학위를 받는 거예요. 학원, 교육 과정, 대학원에는 '수료하다', 학교에는 '졸업하다'를 써요. 대학원에서 '수료'는 수업은 끝났지만 논문은 아직인 상태를 말해요.
explain_en: 수료 means you finished a set program through to the end, while 졸업 means finishing a whole school and receiving a degree. Use 수료하다 for academies, training programs and graduate school, and 졸업하다 for schools. In graduate school, 수료 means coursework is done but the thesis is not.

dis.h: finish a program, without earning a degree

p.n: 이수 stresses completing the required credits; 수료 stresses finishing the whole program.

en: to commercialize; to put to practical use

examples.ko: 이 회사는 새 배터리 기술을 내년에 실용화할 계획이에요.
examples.en: This company plans to put the new battery technology to practical use next year.

examples.ko: 연구만 하지 말고 빨리 실용화해 보면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I wish they would try putting it to practical use soon instead of only researching it.

examples.ko: 그 기술을 실용화하려면 비용을 더 줄여야 해요.
examples.en: To put that technology to practical use, we need to cut the cost further.

examples.ko: 대학 연구팀이 처음으로 이 장치를 실용화했어요.
examples.en: A university research team was the first to put this device to practical use.
It took three years to turn the idea into something practical.

examples.ko: 자율 주행차를 실용화하기까지 아직 시간이 필요해요.
examples.en: It will still take time before self-driving cars are put to practical use.

explain: 연구하거나 발명한 것을 실제 제품이나 서비스로 쓸 수 있게 만들 때 써요. '기술', '제품', '장치' 같은 말과 잘 어울리고 뉴스나 기사에서 자주 보여요. '상용화하다'는 상품으로 팔 수 있게 한다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is used when research or an invention is made usable as a real product or service. It goes well with words like technology, product and device, and often appears in news articles. '상용화하다' has a stronger feel of turning something into a product to sell.

en: to be ambitious; to be aspiring

examples.ko: 신입 사원이 야심만만하게 새 계획을 발표했어요.
examples.en: The new employee ambitiously presented a new plan.

examples.ko: 그 감독은 야심만만해서 늘 큰 영화를 꿈꿔요.
examples.en: That director is ambitious and always dreams of big movies.
Ambitious young people are taking on the challenge of starting businesses.
My younger sibling looks ambitious but is tender inside.
I was full of ambition at first, but reality wasn't easy.

examples.ko: 우리 팀 후배는 팀장 자리를 노릴 만큼 야심만만해요.
examples.en: The junior on our team is so ambitious that he's aiming for the team leader spot.

explain: 큰 목표나 욕심이 가득한 모습이에요. 칭찬일 때도 있고 욕심이 너무 크다는 부정적인 느낌일 때도 있어서 문맥이 중요해요. 비슷한 표현으로 '야심 차다'도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It describes someone full of big goals and desire. It can be praise, but it can also sound negative when the ambition seems too greedy, so context matters. A similar expression that is also common is '야심 차다'.

examples.ko: 그는 언변이 좋아서 사람들을 쉽게 설득해요.
examples.en: He is a good talker, so he persuades people easily.
A person with great speaking skills has an advantage in interviews.

examples.ko: 저는 언변이 없어서 발표가 늘 힘들어요.
examples.en: I'm not good with words, so presentations are always hard.
In sales, sincerity matters more than flashy talk.
That person captivated the audience with natural eloquence.
Speaking skills can improve with practice.

explain: '말솜씨'와 비슷하지만 좀 더 격식 있고 글 같은 느낌이에요. '언변이 좋다/뛰어나다/없다'처럼 짝지어 써요. '화려한 언변'은 말만 번지르르하다는 약간 부정적인 느낌도 줄 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is similar to '말솜씨' but feels a bit more formal and bookish. It pairs as in '언변이 좋다', '언변이 뛰어나다' and '언변이 없다'. '화려한 언변' can also carry a slightly negative sense of being all smooth talk.

examples.en: This company is famous for software engineering.
I want to major in engineering at university.

examples.ko: 엔지니어링 팀이 새 제품을 만들고 있어요.
examples.en: The engineering team is building a new product.
I got a job at a construction engineering firm.
Engineering requires a lot of math.

examples.ko: 그 회사 이름에 엔지니어링이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: The word engineering is in that company's name.

explain: 학문 이름은 '공학'이고, '엔지니어링'은 회사 이름이나 업계에서 더 많이 써요. 사람은 '엔지니어'라고 불러요. 혼자 쓰기보다 '소프트웨어 엔지니어링', '건설 엔지니어링'처럼 앞에 분야가 붙어요.
explain_en: The academic field is '공학', while '엔지니어링' is used more in company names and industry talk. A person is an '엔지니어'. It usually comes with a field before it, like '소프트웨어 엔지니어링' or '건설 엔지니어링'.

en: to be substantial; to be solid

examples.en: This year the apples grew in nice and solid.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 몸집은 작아도 속이 옹골차요.
examples.en: That child is small, but solid on the inside.
I came up to Seoul with a solid dream.
The players went into the game with firm determination.

examples.ko: 이 세트는 구성이 옹골차서 가격보다 훨씬 만족스러워요.
examples.en: This set is so well packed that it's far more satisfying than its price.
He lived his life with substance, so I respect him.

explain: '알차다', '야무지다'와 비슷해요. 사람의 단단하고 야무진 모습에도, 내용이 꽉 찬 물건에도 써요. '옹골차요/옹골찬/옹골차게'처럼 활용해요.
explain_en: It is close to '알차다' and '야무지다'. It describes a person who is firm and capable, and also things that are packed with substance. Typical forms are '옹골차요', '옹골찬', and '옹골차게'.

examples.en: I completed the work I was assigned to the end.
I really want to accomplish this mission.

examples.ko: 선수들은 목표를 완수하기 위해 열심히 훈련해요.
examples.en: The players train hard to achieve their goal.
If you complete the task you promised, you get a reward.

examples.ko: 그는 어려운 과제를 완수한 뒤 휴가를 떠났어요.
examples.en: He went on vacation after completing the hard assignment.
I'm confident I can see it through to the end.

explain: '끝내다'보다 책임이나 임무를 끝까지 해냈다는 무게가 있어요. '임무를 완수하다', '목표를 완수하다'처럼 목적어가 임무, 책임, 목표인 경우가 많아요. 가벼운 일에는 '다 하다', '끝내다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Heavier than 끝내다, it carries the weight of seeing a duty or mission through to the end. Its objects are often 임무, 책임, or 목표. For light tasks, 다 하다 or 끝내다 is more natural.

examples.en: I entered the pre-med course at university this year.
After finishing pre-med, you move up to the medical program.
My younger sibling studies hard to get into pre-med.

examples.ko: 의예과 학생들은 기초 과목을 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Pre-med students take many basic courses.
Admission to pre-med is extremely competitive.
My friend is in pre-med, so they're always busy.

explain: 의과대학에서 본격적인 의학 공부 전에 다니는 첫 과정이에요. 일상에서는 '의대'라고 줄여 말하는 경우가 많은데, '의예과'는 학과 이름이고 '의대'는 단과대학이에요.
explain_en: It is the first stage of a medical college, before the main medical studies. In daily talk people often just say '의대', but '의예과' is the name of the program while '의대' is the college itself.

en: to contribute; to be a help to

examples.en: Small efforts contributed to a big success.
We praised the player who helped the team win.

examples.ko: 환경 보호에 일조하고 싶어서 텀블러를 써요.
examples.en: I use a tumbler because I want to do my part for the environment.

examples.ko: 우리 가게가 지역 발전에 일조할 수 있으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope our shop can contribute to the development of the area.

examples.ko: 봉사 활동이 사회 분위기를 바꾸는 데 일조해요.
examples.en: Volunteer work helps change the mood of society.

examples.ko: 자원봉사자들이 행사 성공에 일조하는 모습이 보기 좋았어요.
examples.en: It was nice to see the volunteers helping make the event a success.

explain: '~에 일조하다'꼴로 써요. 큰 일의 일부를 맡아서 도움이 된다는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '도움이 되다', '한몫하다'라고 하고, '일조하다'는 격식 있는 글이나 연설에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used in the pattern '~에 일조하다', for helping a larger effort by playing a part in it. In daily speech people say '도움이 되다' or '한몫하다', while '일조하다' is common in formal writing and speeches.

dis.h: play a small helping part; formal

p.s: 이 책은 학생들의 성적 향상에 일조했다.
p.o: 이 책은 학생들의 성적 향상에 기여했다.
p.n: 일조 suggests a modest share of the help; 기여 is neutral.

en: to be formally appointed (to a public post)

examples.en: He was appointed as a middle school teacher this year.
To be appointed, you must first pass the exam.
The newly appointed teacher said hello today.
I was appointed as a civil servant and got my first paycheck.
I can't wait for the day I'm appointed at city hall.

examples.ko: 이번 달에 임용될 사람은 모두 열 명이에요.
examples.en: Ten people in all will be appointed this month.

explain: '채용되다'는 회사에서 쓰는 일반적인 말이고, '임용되다'는 공무원, 교사, 교수처럼 나라나 학교가 정식으로 자리를 줄 때 써요. '교원 임용 시험'처럼 시험 이름에도 나와요.
explain_en: '채용되다' is the general word for being hired at a company, while '임용되다' is used when the state or a school formally gives someone a post, such as a civil servant, teacher or professor. It also appears in exam names like '교원 임용 시험'.

examples.en: All of our company's products are made in Korea.
I explained our company's history to the new employees.

examples.ko: 이 보고서는 자사의 매출을 정리한 거예요.
examples.en: This report summarizes our company's sales.
You can sign up on our company website.

examples.ko: 다른 회사보다 자사 서비스가 더 빨라요.
examples.en: Our own service is faster than other companies'.

examples.ko: 기자가 자사 기사를 먼저 내보내고 싶다고 했어요.
examples.en: The reporter said he wanted to run his own company's article first.

explain: 자사는 말하는 사람이 속한 회사를 가리켜요. 회사 안이나 뉴스, 공문에서 '우리 회사' 대신 쓰는 딱딱한 말이라 친구와 이야기할 때는 거의 안 써요. 남의 회사는 '타사'라고 해요.
explain_en: 자사 refers to the speaker's own company. It is a formal word used in business documents and news instead of '우리 회사', and you rarely hear it in casual talk. A competitor's company is '타사'.

examples.en: I learned how to make kimchi from my grandmother.
They say he was taught pottery skills by his master.
I came back to my hometown to take over the family business.
After being taught the secret recipe, I opened a restaurant.

examples.ko: 이 춤은 어떻게 전수받을 수 있어요?
examples.en: How can I learn this dance from a master?
I make a living with the skill I was taught by my father.

explain: 그냥 '배우다'보다 스승이나 윗사람에게서 기술이나 비법을 이어받는 느낌이 강해요. 가르쳐 주는 사람 쪽은 '전수하다'라고 해요. 보통 '~에게/께 ~을 전수받다'로 써요.
explain_en: Compared with plain '배우다', it feels like inheriting a skill or secret from a master or an elder. The person who teaches uses '전수하다'. The usual pattern is '~에게/께 ~을 전수받다'.

examples.en: That teacher is well versed in Korean history.
I asked a friend who knows computers inside out for help.

examples.ko: 그는 동네 맛집에 정통해서 어디든 추천해 줘요.
examples.en: He knows the local restaurants so well that he can recommend anywhere.

examples.ko: 저는 요리에 정통하지 않아서 레시피를 봐요.
examples.en: I'm not an expert at cooking, so I follow a recipe.
He is a professor with a reputation for knowing this field thoroughly.
He is well known for being an expert on Korean movies.

explain: '~에 정통하다'처럼 '에'와 함께 써요. 어떤 분야를 깊이 아는 사람을 칭찬할 때 쓰는 격식 있는 말이라서, 친구끼리는 '~를 잘 알아요'라고 더 많이 해요. '능통하다'는 외국어나 기술을 능숙하게 쓸 때 써요(영어에 능통하다).
explain_en: It is used as '~에 정통하다', with the particle 에. It is a fairly formal way to praise someone who knows a field deeply; friends more often just say '~를 잘 알아요'. 능통하다 is different: it is for being fluent in a language or skilled at using a technique (영어에 능통하다).

examples.ko: 요리는 제 주특기라고 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You could say cooking is my specialty.
That player's specialty is quick dribbling.

examples.ko: 면접에서 제 주특기를 살려서 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: In the interview, I showed off my specialty.
Telling jokes has become Dad's specialty.
I'll make you my specialty, rolled omelet.
This time I'm going to compete with my best skill.

explain: '특기'보다 '가장 자신 있는 것'이라는 느낌이 강해요. 친구끼리는 농담처럼 '그건 내 주특기지!'라고도 해요. 군대에서는 맡은 일의 종류를 '주특기'라고 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: Compared with '특기', it has a stronger sense of 'the thing I'm most confident at'. Friends also say it jokingly, like '그건 내 주특기지!'. In the military, '주특기' is also the name for a soldier's assigned job type.

examples.en: Regular exercise improves your health.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 우호를 증진하기 위해 만났어요.
examples.en: The two countries met to promote friendship.

examples.ko: 비타민은 면역력을 증진하는 데 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Vitamins help boost immunity.

examples.ko: 이 프로그램은 아이들의 학습 능력을 증진해 줘요.
examples.en: This program improves children's learning ability.
There is research saying walking improves stamina.

examples.ko: 건강을 증진하고 싶으면 잠을 충분히 자요.
examples.en: If you want to improve your health, get enough sleep.

explain: 건강, 체력, 복지, 친선처럼 좋은 것을 더 좋아지게 할 때 써요. '늘리다'는 수나 양에 두루 쓰지만 '증진하다'는 건강·능력·관계 같은 말과 주로 어울려요. 뉴스와 안내문에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Use it when you make something good even better, such as health, stamina, welfare, or friendly relations. '늘리다' works for any number or amount, while '증진하다' mostly goes with health, ability, and relationships. You see it often in news and notices.
